record.paper_title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
record.original_question: Can the convergence and worst-case iteration-complexity results established for proximal quasi-Newton trust-region and quadratic-regularization methods in nonsmooth regularized optimization be extended to cubic regularization variants?

evidence.quote: extensions of our results to cubic regularization

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the composite optimization problem
    minimize_{x ∈ ℝ^n}  φ(x) := f(x) + h(x),
where f : ℝ^n → ℝ is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and h : ℝ^n → ℝ ∪ {+∞} is proper, lower semicontinuous, and prox-bounded (possibly nonconvex and nonsmooth). A proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method generates iterates x_k by approximately minimizing, over a trust region of radius Δ_k, a model
    m_k(s) = f(x_k) + ⟨∇f(x_k), s⟩ + (1/2)⟨s, B_k s⟩ + h(x_k + s),
where B_k is a symmetric quasi-Newton approximation to ∇^2 f(x_k). The closely related proximal quadratic-regularization variant replaces the trust-region constraint by an added term (σ_k/2)‖s‖^2 in the model, with adaptive σ_k > 0. For both schemes, under standard assumptions on f, h, and {B_k}, global convergence to first-order stationary points (in the sense that a suitable proximal stationarity measure tends to zero) and worst-case iteration complexity bounds of the form O(ε^{-2}) for driving this stationarity measure below ε > 0 are known.

Now consider the cubic regularization analogue, in which the step at iteration k is computed as an approximate minimizer of
    m_k^{cubic}(s) = f(x_k) + ⟨∇f(x_k), s⟩ + (1/2)⟨s, B_k s⟩ + (σ_k/3)‖s‖^3 + h(x_k + s),
with σ_k > 0 updated adaptively according to the achieved-versus-predicted reduction in φ.

Question: Can one establish, for this proximal quasi-Newton cubic-regularization method, global convergence to first-order stationary points together with a worst-case iteration complexity bound (analogous to the O(ε^{-3/2}) bounds known for smooth cubic regularization) for driving the proximal stationarity measure below ε?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has developed inexact q-order regularized proximal Newton methods for nonconvex composite problems (SIAM J. Optim. 2024) and proximal modified quasi-Newton schemes (R2N) with tight worst-case complexity bounds, addressing higher-order regularization variants of the proximal quasi-Newton framework. While these results suggest cubic-regularization extensions are feasible and partially realized for related proximal Newton-type methods, a complete cubic-regularization analogue specifically of the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region/quadratic-regularization framework with matching convergence and complexity guarantees does not appear to be fully established in a single unified treatment.

status_evidence.title: An Inexact q-Order Regularized Proximal Newton Method for Nonconvex Composite Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Develops inexact q-order (including cubic) regularized proximal Newton methods for nonconvex and nonsmooth composite problems with complexity analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order (including cubic) regularized proximal Newton methods for nonsmooth composite optimization have been studied with convergence and complexity results.

status_evidence.title: A Proximal Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: R2N is a modified quasi-Newton method with tight worst-case complexity bounds O(ε^{-2/(1-p)}) for the proximal stationarity measure.
status_evidence.claim: Quadratic-regularization proximal quasi-Newton methods now have established tight complexity bounds, but the analysis is not stated in cubic-regularization form.
